narrative:
The 2025 Colorado Rockies were a team that never found its footing, stumbling out of the gate and never recovering. From the very first week of the season, opposing hitters punished a thin and overmatched pitching staff, setting the tone for what would become one of the most difficult seasons in franchise history. A 43-119 record tells the story bluntly: this was a team outscored by 424 runs, surrendering over a thousand across 162 games while struggling to manufacture offense against quality competition.

The early months were defined almost entirely by pitching collapses. Relievers like Victor Vodnik and Seth Halvorsen were repeatedly victimized, giving up game-changing hits and home runs that buried the Rockies before they could ever mount a comeback. The lone bright spot in April came on the 22nd, when catcher Jacob Stallings cracked a sharp two-run double that gave Colorado a fleeting sense of life. But those moments were the exception, not the rule, as the bullpen continued to bleed runs night after night.

The summer months offered a handful of individual highlights that provided brief relief from the losing. Mickey Moniak emerged as a bright young presence, clubbing back-to-back home runs in June, while Brenton Doyle delivered the season's most impactful positive play with a two-run shot on August 1st. Hunter Goodman continued to develop, launching his 24th home run in mid-August to give the Coors Field faithful something to cheer. These performances pointed toward potential building blocks for the future even as the losses continued to pile up relentlessly.

By September, the narrative had fully settled into one of endurance rather than competition. Victor Vodnik's ongoing struggles were punctuated by a brutal late-season double allowed in the final weeks, a fitting if painful symbol of a year that tested everyone in the organization. The Rockies finished 43-119, a record that will demand significant roster reconstruction and a clear-eyed reckoning with the franchise's long-term direction. The silver linings — Moniak's power, Goodman's growth, Doyle's athleticism — will need to be the foundation upon which something better is built.

chapters.title: Disaster From the Start
chapters.description: The Rockies open the season with immediate pitching meltdowns and costly surrendered hits, signaling the painful year ahead.

chapters.title: A Rare Flicker of Hope
chapters.description: Jacob Stallings delivers a clutch two-run double in late April, offering one of the season's few genuine bright moments before the bullpen squanders it.

chapters.title: May Misery
chapters.description: Grand slams, double plays, and home runs allowed define a brutal May stretch that erases any optimism and deepens the Rockies' descent.

chapters.title: Summer Sparks
chapters.description: Amid continued losses, Mickey Moniak and Orlando Arcia provide offensive highlights in June and July that give fans something to celebrate.

chapters.title: Individual Heroics in a Lost Cause
chapters.description: Brenton Doyle and Hunter Goodman deliver standout offensive moments in August, showcasing the team's few legitimate building blocks for the future.

chapters.title: Limping to the Finish
chapters.description: The final weeks bring more of the same suffering as the bullpen falters again in September, closing the curtain on a historically difficult season.
